title: Type Cosplay Vulnerability Solana Anchor
text:
Type Cosplay Vulnerability in Solana Anchor Programs

Description:
Type cosplay occurs when one account type is substituted for another without
proper discriminator verification. An attacker can pass a maliciously crafted
account that has the same data layout as the expected account type.

Vulnerable pattern:
```rust
#[derive(Accounts)]
pub struct UpdateUser<'info> {
    user: Account<'info, User>,  // No discriminator check
    admin: Account<'info, User>, // Could be passed a non-admin account
}
```

The problem: Anchor Account<'info, T> checks owner but not the discriminator
by default in older versions. Any account owned by the program passes.

Secure pattern:
```rust
#[account]
pub struct User {
    discriminant: AccountDiscriminant,  // Add discriminant field
    authority: Pubkey,
}

#[derive(AnchorSerialize, AnchorDeserialize, PartialEq)]
pub enum AccountDiscriminant {
    User,
    Admin,
}

// In function:
require!(
    user.discriminant == AccountDiscriminant::User,
    ErrorCode::InvalidDiscriminant
);
```

Anchor fix: Use #[account(discriminator = ...)] or check discriminant field manually.
Detection: Look for Account<'info, T> without discriminator field in struct.
Source: Sealevel Attacks #3, Neodyme Pitfalls

Type Cosplay Account Substitution Vulnerability Solana

Type cosplay discriminator attack: attacker substitutes one account type for another.
Without discriminator checks, Account<'info, Admin> accepts User account data.

Vulnerable code:
pub struct UpdateAdmin {
    user: Account<'info, User>,   // No discriminant field check
}
pub struct User { authority: Pubkey, balance: u64 }
pub struct Admin { authority: Pubkey, balance: u64 }  // Same layout!

Attack: pass Admin account where User expected, bypass access control.

Fix with discriminant field:
#[account]
pub struct User {
    discriminant: AccountDiscriminant,
    authority: Pubkey,
}
pub enum AccountDiscriminant { User, Admin }

require!(user.discriminant == AccountDiscriminant::User, ErrorCode::InvalidAccount);

Anchor 8-byte discriminator: Anchor automatically prepends 8-byte discriminator.
Account<'info, T> checks discriminator automatically in Anchor >= 0.20.
But AccountInfo does NOT check discriminator.

Detection pattern: AccountInfo used where Account<T> expected for typed accounts.
Fix: Use Account<'info, T> not AccountInfo for typed accounts.
Source: Sealevel attacks program 3-type-cosplay
